Probe results, 2026-11-07 (grok 1.0.77, Linux, one call each, in a throwaway repo under .scratch/grok-probe/; outputs in .scratch/grok-probe/out/). The permission rules in --allow are Claude-style and work headless: (1) --permission-mode dontAsk, acceptEdits and plan, each with --allow 'Bash(go test*)', ran go test and reported the result (p1, p4, p5). (2) --permission-mode dontAsk with --allow write --allow search_replace (Grok's own tool names) appended a line to notes.txt inside the repo (q1); --allow Edit --allow Write did not get used for the edit (the model tried a shell append, which was denied, p2). So the write rule names are Grok's tool names, write and search_replace. Containment is NOT provided by these rules: (3) with --allow write the model wrote a file OUTSIDE the working directory (r1, outside.txt changed to 'hacked'; same with --allow Write in p6). (4) dontAsk is not a strict allowlist: with only write and search_replace allowed, 'touch made-by-shell.txt' ran (r2), and 'git log -1' ran with only go test allowed (q2); a compound shell command with a redirect (printf >> notes.txt && tail) was denied (p2). (5) --sandbox workspace needs bubblewrap, which is not installed on this host (q3 to q6 exit 1: 'bwrap exec failed ... Install bubblewrap'); the sandbox cells are therefore untested, with and without --always-approve. Open for the owner: accept the same containment stance as decision 100 for Codex (rely on the tree fingerprint, the project check, review and the gate, and on bubblewrap plus --sandbox where installed), or hold grok write roles until the sandbox is probed on a host that has bubblewrap. Grok rule syntax to build from: --allow 'Bash(go test*)' style for commands and --allow write / search_replace for edits; ork would pass the role's allowlist from internal/engine/perm.go, mapping Claude's Edit and Write to these tool names.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). Containment: Grok write roles take the same stance as Codex (decision 100): ork relies on the tree fingerprint, the project check, review and the gate as the limits, with --allow rules built from the role's allowlist in internal/engine/perm.go (Grok tool names write and search_replace for edits, Bash(...) rules for commands). The owner installs bubblewrap on their machine; ork then adds --sandbox, which is probed on a host that has it (a follow-up slice). Reviewer, gate and spec-check roles on Grok get --allow rules for their read-only test and slicer commands in plan mode. Record this as an adj question first (the owner decides it); the S72 ruling against write roles is superseded for all grok.

Evidence from the S274 relay, 2026-11-07: a Grok reviewer in headless plan mode ran with --allow 'Bash(go test*)' --allow 'Bash(go -C * test*)' --allow 'Bash(go vet*)' --allow 'Bash(go -C * vet*)' --allow 'Bash(gofmt*)' --allow 'Bash(slicer show*)' --allow 'Bash(slicer goals*)' and executed go test -race per package, go vet and gofmt, and returned a real review with a VERDICT line (two rounds). Without those rules the same role was denied a piped slicer call and go test and returned no report. Commands must be run alone: pipes, redirects and && are still denied. Keep this as the starting rule set for ork's Grok read-only roles.
